top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a new way of holding thousands of atoms Doppler- and recoil-free with the clock transition unperturbed, removing the single-ion signal-to-noise limit. It is reproduced and compared across independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) at the 1e-18 level, with systematic shifts calculated and then checked experimentally, and it has enabled millimetre-scale redshift tests and tighter bounds on constants. The two-name attribution is the cleanest available and the P002 citation is confined to the lattice clock, keeping the 2005 comb and 2012 ion work untouched. Magic-angle graphene (P001) is a strong second, a confirmed prediction with a new state of matter, but the three-name cut leaves the Cao, Fatemi, Dean and earlier flat-band attribution questions open; any award is preferred to none.
recusal_note: During my PhD I spent a year in John Hall's laboratory at JILA, where Jun Ye (credited in P002) later worked; no collaboration, financial tie or recent contact with Ye or Katori that I know of, so I do not see grounds for recusal, but I note it. My WACQT role overlaps institutionally with Chalmers (circuit QED), which is not in this slate.
